The present disclosure may be applied to intelligent services based on 5G communication technology and IoT-related technology, including smart homes, smart buildings, smart cities, smart cars, connected cars, healthcare, digital education, smart retail, security, and safety services.

Specifically, the present disclosure defines an in-band mode operation of an LTE-lite terminal to avoid collision with a conventional LTE terminal, and provides, among other things, a method for using a reference signal and a method for periodically puncturing a specific slot.

This disclosure concerns a communication technique and system that integrate an Internet of Things (IoT) technology with a 5th-Generation (5G) communication system designed to provide data rates higher than those of a 4th-Generation (4G) system. The disclosure can be used for intelligent services built on 5G communication technology and IoT-related technologies, including smart homes, smart buildings, smart cities, smart cars, connected vehicles, healthcare, digital education, smart retail, and security and safety services.

More specifically, the disclosure is directed to a wireless communication system, and in particular to an apparatus and method for sending or receiving a synchronization signal, a physical broadcast channel, a control signal, and a data signal in a system that supports transmission and reception over a narrowband channel of approximately 180 kHz. In detail, the disclosure specifies in-band mode operation for an LTE-lite terminal so as to prevent collisions with a legacy LTE terminal, and also presents techniques such as a method for utilizing a reference signal and a method for periodically puncturing a designated slot.
outputs.L3:
The present disclosure relates to a communication method and system that integrates fifth-generation (5G) communication technology with Internet of Things (IoT) technologies. More particularly, the disclosure addresses techniques for enabling efficient wireless communication between network devices and low-complexity terminals in environments where a large number of connected devices may be deployed. By combining the high-capacity, low-latency, and flexible networking capabilities of 5G systems with IoT-based device connectivity, the disclosed technology may support a wide range of intelligent and automated services.

The disclosed technology may be applied to various intelligent service fields, including, but not limited to, smart homes, smart buildings, smart cities, connected vehicles, health care systems, digital education platforms, and smart retail or security services. For example, in a smart home environment, the technology may be used to connect sensors, appliances, access-control devices, and monitoring systems. In a smart city environment, it may support infrastructure monitoring, public safety systems, traffic control, utility management, and environmental sensing. In connected-car applications, the technology may facilitate communication between vehicles, roadside infrastructure, and network servers. In health care and education, the technology may be used to support remote monitoring, interactive learning, and connected service platforms. In retail and security environments, it may enable inventory tracking, surveillance, authentication, and automated response systems.

The disclosure particularly focuses on wireless communication methods and apparatuses for transmitting and receiving synchronization signals, broadcast channels, control signals, and data signals. These signals may be used by a terminal to detect a cell, acquire timing and frequency synchronization, receive system information, monitor control information, and exchange user data with a base station or other network node. The described methods may improve communication reliability and resource efficiency, especially for terminals having reduced bandwidth capability or reduced complexity compared with conventional broadband mobile terminals.

In one aspect, the system supports transmission and reception through a narrowband channel having a bandwidth of approximately 180 kHz. Such a narrowband configuration may be suitable for IoT terminals, machine-type communication devices, or LTE-lite terminals that transmit relatively small amounts of data and require low power consumption, extended coverage, and reduced hardware complexity. By limiting communication to a narrow bandwidth, the terminal may reduce power usage and implementation cost while still maintaining connectivity with a cellular network.

The disclosure further defines in-band operation for an LTE-lite terminal within a wider LTE carrier. In this operating mode, the LTE-lite terminal communicates using a narrowband region that is included within the bandwidth of a conventional LTE system. To enable coexistence with conventional LTE terminals, the disclosure provides techniques for avoiding collisions between transmissions intended for LTE-lite terminals and transmissions intended for legacy LTE terminals. These techniques may include specific methods for using reference signals, determining resource locations, and coordinating transmissions so that LTE-lite signaling does not interfere with existing LTE downlink or uplink structures.

In addition, the disclosure describes the use of periodic slot puncturing. Through periodic slot puncturing, certain portions of a transmission slot may be reserved, muted, or otherwise made unavailable for LTE-lite transmission in order to accommodate reference signals, control channels, or other signals used by conventional LTE terminals. This allows LTE-lite terminals to operate in-band while preserving compatibility with legacy LTE operation. The puncturing pattern may be configured or predefined so that the LTE-lite terminal can identify usable and unusable resource regions and can properly receive synchronization, broadcast, control, and data signals.

Accordingly, the disclosed communication method and system provide a framework for supporting low-complexity, narrowband IoT communication within an existing LTE or 5G-related cellular environment. By enabling efficient transmission and reception of essential wireless signals over a narrowband channel and by defining coexistence mechanisms for in-band LTE-lite operation, the technology may improve network resource utilization, reduce terminal complexity and power consumption, and support scalable deployment of intelligent IoT services.
outputs.L4:
The disclosure relates to wireless communication systems, and in particular to techniques for supporting fifth generation (5G), Internet of Things (IoT), machine-type communication (MTC), or LTE-lite operation over a narrowband carrier or narrowband portion of a wider carrier. In one example, the narrowband channel may have a bandwidth of approximately 180 kHz, corresponding to one physical resource block in an LTE system. The proposed techniques enable low-complexity terminals to communicate efficiently while using reduced bandwidth, reduced processing capability, and reduced power consumption compared with conventional wideband LTE user equipment.

According to the disclosure, methods and apparatuses are provided for transmitting and receiving synchronization signals, broadcast information, control signaling, and user data over the narrowband channel. A base station may generate and transmit synchronization signals that allow a narrowband terminal to acquire time and frequency synchronization with the network. The base station may also transmit system information or broadcast information in a format suitable for reception by a terminal that monitors only the narrowband channel. The terminal may then receive control information identifying resources, modulation and coding schemes, repetitions, or scheduling assignments, and may transmit or receive data according to the indicated configuration.

The disclosure further describes operation of an in-band LTE-lite terminal within a conventional LTE carrier. In such an arrangement, the narrowband terminal operates using only a small portion of the LTE system bandwidth while sharing the carrier with legacy LTE terminals. Because legacy LTE signals, including reference signals and control channels, may already occupy certain time-frequency resources, the disclosure provides mechanisms for avoiding or reducing interference and collisions between LTE-lite transmissions and conventional LTE transmissions.

For example, the LTE-lite terminal may be configured to use selected LTE reference signals for synchronization, channel estimation, measurements, or demodulation. The terminal may identify cell-specific reference signals, narrowband reference signals, or other pilot structures and use them according to its reduced-bandwidth capability. In some embodiments, reference signals may be transmitted or interpreted differently for narrowband operation so that reliable channel estimation can be achieved without requiring the terminal to process the entire LTE bandwidth.

The disclosure also defines periodic slot puncturing or muting techniques. In such techniques, certain slots, subframes, symbols, or resource elements within the narrowband channel may be left unused, punctured, or reserved to prevent overlap with signals intended for conventional LTE terminals. By periodically puncturing narrowband transmissions, the system may preserve compatibility with existing LTE operation while still providing predictable opportunities for LTE-lite synchronization, broadcast, control, and data communication. The puncturing pattern may be predefined, configured by higher-layer signaling, or indicated through broadcast or control information.

In operation, a base station may determine a narrowband region within an LTE carrier and configure that region for LTE-lite or IoT communication. The base station may transmit narrowband synchronization and broadcast signals using resources that are compatible with the LTE frame structure. A narrowband terminal may search for the synchronization signal, decode broadcast information, determine the applicable resource configuration and puncturing pattern, and then monitor narrowband control channels for scheduling information. Based on the received control information, the terminal may receive downlink data or transmit uplink data using the assigned narrowband resources.

The disclosed methods may support repetitions, robust coding, and simplified signaling to improve coverage and reliability, which are especially useful for IoT devices located indoors, underground, or at the edge of a cell. The narrowband operation may also reduce terminal complexity by allowing the terminal to employ a smaller radio-frequency bandwidth, simplified baseband processing, and lower sampling rates. This can reduce cost and extend battery life, making the techniques suitable for sensors, meters, tracking devices, alarms, industrial controllers, and other low-data-rate wireless devices.

The disclosure therefore provides a framework for efficient narrowband communication within or alongside an LTE-based system. By defining how synchronization, broadcast, control, reference, and data signals are transmitted and received over an approximately 180 kHz channel, and by specifying in-band operation techniques such as reference signal usage and periodic slot puncturing, the system can support LTE-lite and IoT terminals without disrupting conventional LTE users. This enables scalable narrowband connectivity, improved spectrum reuse, and backward-compatible deployment of low-power wide-area communication services.
outputs.L5:
**The Internet Generation**

The Internet has changed the way people live, learn, and communicate. Today’s young people are often called the Internet Generation because they have grown up with digital technology all around them. For many of them, using the Internet is a normal part of everyday life.

The Internet Generation uses online tools for education, entertainment, shopping, and social interaction. Students can find information quickly, watch educational videos, and communicate with teachers and classmates from anywhere. Social media also allows people to stay connected with friends and family, even across long distances.

However, the Internet also brings challenges. Spending too much time online can affect health, concentration, and real-life relationships. There are also risks such as misinformation, cyberbullying, and loss of privacy. Because of this, it is important for people to use the Internet responsibly and think carefully about what they read and share online.

In conclusion, the Internet Generation has many opportunities that previous generations did not have. The Internet can be a powerful tool for learning, creativity, and connection. But to benefit from it fully, people must use it wisely and balance their online and offline lives.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style technical field/background paragraph for an invention about LTE-lite narrowband 180 kHz communication in a 5G/IoT wireless system, including synchronization signals, PBCH, control/data signals, in-band operation, collision avoidance with LTE terminals, reference signals, and periodic slot puncturing.
counterfactuals.output: The present disclosure relates generally to wireless communication systems, and more particularly to techniques for supporting low-complexity and/or low-power Internet of Things (IoT) devices using an LTE-lite narrowband carrier, for example a 180 kHz resource bandwidth, within a fifth generation (5G) or evolved cellular radio access network. In certain deployments, a narrowband communication channel may be operated in-band within a wider LTE or 5G carrier and may convey synchronization signals, a physical broadcast channel (PBCH), control signaling, and user data signaling to enable reduced-bandwidth terminals to acquire timing, obtain system information, receive scheduling assignments, and exchange data with a base station. However, in-band narrowband operation presents technical challenges including coexistence with legacy LTE terminals, avoidance of collisions with LTE physical channels and reference signals, maintenance of reliable channel estimation through appropriate narrowband reference signals, and accommodation of time-frequency resources reserved or occupied by wideband system transmissions. Accordingly, there is a need for mechanisms that map LTE-lite synchronization signals, PBCH, control channels, data channels, and reference signals into the 180 kHz narrowband while avoiding interference with LTE terminals and legacy reference signal patterns, including techniques such as periodic slot puncturing or muting of selected narrowband resources to prevent collisions with LTE control, synchronization, broadcast, or reference signal transmissions while preserving robust narrowband coverage and efficient IoT communication.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft an abstract-like disclosure section for a telecommunications patent concerning a method and device for transmitting and receiving signals over a narrowband channel in LTE/5G IoT systems.
counterfactuals.output:
A method and apparatus are disclosed for transmitting and receiving signals over a narrowband channel in a wireless communication system, including an LTE, LTE-M, NB-IoT, or 5G IoT network. A user equipment (UE) may receive configuration information from a base station indicating one or more narrowband resources within a system bandwidth, a subcarrier spacing, a repetition level, a modulation and coding scheme, and/or a time-frequency hopping pattern. The UE may transmit or receive a physical control channel, a physical data channel, or a reference signal using the configured narrowband resources.

In one embodiment, the UE determines a narrowband transmission occasion based on a resource allocation parameter and maps uplink or downlink symbols to a plurality of resource elements within the narrowband channel. The mapped symbols may be repeated across multiple subframes, slots, or mini-slots to improve coverage for low-power or extended-coverage devices. The UE may further apply frequency hopping between different narrowband regions to reduce interference and improve frequency diversity.

A base station may generate and transmit control signaling that identifies the narrowband channel and associated transmission parameters. The base station may receive an uplink signal from the UE or transmit a downlink signal to the UE using the identified narrowband resources, and may combine repeated transmissions to decode the signal. Reference signals may be inserted according to a narrowband-specific pattern to support channel estimation, synchronization, and demodulation.

The disclosed techniques enable efficient communication for IoT devices operating with reduced bandwidth, reduced complexity, and limited power consumption, while maintaining compatibility with wideband LTE or 5G carrier deployments. The method may be implemented in a UE, a base station, or circuitry comprising one or more processors and memory storing instructions that, when executed, cause the device to perform the described transmission and reception operations.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate formal patent language beginning with “The present disclosure relates to…” for a wireless communication invention that combines 5G and IoT technologies and supports LTE-lite terminals operating in-band without colliding with legacy LTE terminals.
counterfactuals.output:
The present disclosure relates to wireless communication systems, methods, apparatuses, and computer-readable media for supporting coexistence of fifth-generation (5G) communication technologies and Internet-of-Things (IoT) devices in a cellular network, and more particularly to techniques for enabling LTE-lite terminals to operate in-band within a carrier or spectrum allocation shared with legacy Long Term Evolution (LTE) terminals while reducing, avoiding, or preventing transmission collisions and interference therebetween.

In certain embodiments, a network node, such as a base station, evolved NodeB, next-generation NodeB, or integrated access node, is configured to allocate radio resources within an LTE-compatible carrier for use by one or more reduced-capability IoT terminals, including LTE-lite terminals, while concurrently maintaining service for one or more legacy LTE terminals. The allocated radio resources may comprise time-domain, frequency-domain, code-domain, spatial-domain, or beam-domain resources that are selected based at least in part on scheduling information associated with the legacy LTE terminals, capability information associated with the LTE-lite terminals, traffic type, latency requirements, coverage enhancement requirements, or network load conditions.

In some embodiments, the wireless communication system provides an in-band IoT operating region within a legacy LTE carrier, wherein the in-band IoT operating region is dynamically or semi-statically configured so as not to overlap with resources scheduled for legacy LTE control or data transmissions. The network node may transmit configuration signaling indicating at least one of a narrowband resource location, a subframe pattern, a repetition pattern, a guard resource, a muted resource, or a collision-avoidance rule applicable to the LTE-lite terminals. The LTE-lite terminals may thereafter perform uplink or downlink communication using the indicated resources without colliding with transmissions of the legacy LTE terminals.

In further embodiments, a scheduling entity determines whether a candidate resource for an LTE-lite terminal conflicts with a physical downlink control channel, physical downlink shared channel, physical uplink shared channel, reference signal, synchronization signal, broadcast channel, or hybrid automatic repeat request resource associated with a legacy LTE terminal. Responsive to determining a potential conflict, the scheduling entity may shift, puncture, defer, repeat, narrow, beamform, or otherwise modify the LTE-lite transmission to preserve compatibility with the legacy LTE terminal. In this manner, the LTE-lite terminal can be supported in-band without requiring a dedicated carrier and without materially degrading legacy LTE operation.

The present disclosure further provides mechanisms for 5G-assisted coordination of LTE-lite IoT communications, including network slicing, low-complexity device access, massive machine-type communication support, flexible numerology adaptation, edge-assisted scheduling, and interference-aware resource orchestration. In certain implementations, a 5G control function or core network entity may exchange device capability information, traffic predictions, or policy information with an LTE radio access node to coordinate resource allocation for IoT terminals operating in an LTE in-band region.

According to one aspect, a method performed by a network node comprises identifying a set of legacy LTE terminals served on a carrier; identifying a set of LTE-lite terminals configured for in-band operation on the carrier; determining protected resources associated with the set of legacy LTE terminals; selecting, from remaining available resources of the carrier, one or more communication resources for at least one LTE-lite terminal; transmitting configuration information indicating the selected communication resources to the at least one LTE-lite terminal; and communicating with the at least one LTE-lite terminal using the selected communication resources while avoiding collision with transmissions associated with the legacy LTE terminals.

According to another aspect, an LTE-lite terminal comprises processing circuitry configured to receive configuration information identifying in-band resources within an LTE carrier, determine whether a scheduled transmission opportunity is permitted based on collision-avoidance information included in or derived from the configuration information, and transmit or receive IoT data using the in-band resources only when the scheduled transmission opportunity does not conflict with protected legacy LTE resources.

According to yet another aspect, a wireless communication apparatus comprises at least one processor and memory storing instructions that, when executed by the at least one processor, cause the apparatus to coordinate 5G-IoT resource scheduling with LTE in-band coexistence, classify LTE resources as legacy-protected resources or LTE-lite-available resources, and generate scheduling grants for LTE-lite terminals using the LTE-lite-available resources.

By virtue of the disclosed techniques, reduced-capability IoT terminals may be efficiently deployed within existing LTE spectrum while benefiting from 5G network coordination, improved spectral utilization, reduced interference, enhanced coexistence with legacy LTE terminals, and scalable support for massive IoT communication.
